clue.text: Ruin simple mechanical part in kitchen appliance

parts.note: to dish someone's hopes is to ruin them
a washer is a flat ring, about the plainest component in any machine

explanation.surface: Someone complains that one cheap little component has broken their kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine for cleaning plates is a standard piece of kitchen equipment, so it is an example of an appliance.

clue.text: Obligation of first appearance leaving university

indicators.note: the university goes away, taken out of the first appearance

parts.note: a debut is a first public appearance

explanation.surface: A graduate's first appearance after leaving university brings a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed is a liability, something one is bound to repay.

clue.text: Get rid of journalist that's played violin badly

parts.note: to scrap something is to get rid of it
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone wants rid of a reporter whose fiddle-playing was dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor violinist draws the bow roughly across the strings, a grating sound.

clue.text: Speaking enthusiastically of disc with song Los Angeles rejected

parts.note: a waxing is an old word for a gramophone record
a lyric is the words of a song

indicators.note: rejected things are thrown back, so the city abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone raves about a record with a song turned down by Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means talking about something with great enthusiasm and gushing praise.

clue.text: Blade — I am just the thing to open old wound

indicators.note: the scar is opened up, with the other words inserted within it

parts.note: a scar is the mark of an old wound
I'm is the contraction of I am
it means exactly what is needed, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A blade boasts that it is perfect for reopening an old wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved oriental sword is a type of blade.

clue.text: Presley with energy overwhelming island's little folk

indicators.note: energy overwhelms the island and takes its place in the singer's name

parts.note: Elvis Presley, the American rock and roll singer
I is the abbreviation for island
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An energetic Elvis swamps an island of tiny people.
explanation.definitionFit: Small magical beings of folklore are often called the little folk.

clue.text: Unwanted messages and plans sent back

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the word for plans is read from right to left

parts.note: maps are plans or charts of a place

explanation.surface: An office worker complains about junk emails and returned plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk email is the everyday meaning of the term, named after a tinned meat sketch in Monty Python.

clue.text: Churchman to talk at length about the Spanish

indicators.note: the talking surrounds, or goes about, the Spanish article

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A cleric is long-winded about the Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or other senior cleric is a high-ranking churchman.

clue.text: Quiz in which dimmest ran out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quiz show from which the least clever contestant fled.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the long-running BBC television quiz with a black chair and specialist subjects.

clue.text: Mineral gunners kept in container

indicators.note: one thing kept in another sits inside it, so the gunners go within the container

parts.note: a box is a container
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Artillerymen store some mineral in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium borate is a white crystalline mineral used in cleaning products, so it is an example of a mineral.

clue.text: Fashionable French writer takes ship for northern city

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
Jules Verne, French author of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A trendy French novelist boards a ship bound for a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is only a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of the Scottish Highlands, about as far north as British cities go.

clue.text: Getting back in control before declaration

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second in the answer

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
a statement is a declaration

explanation.surface: Taking back power ahead of an official announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in control' looks like one phrase; 'in' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoration to a former post means getting back in after being removed.

clue.text: 'Topple Tunisia' ordered Roman governor

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, so the quoted words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quoted command to bring down a North African state.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the prefect of Judaea under Tiberius who presided at the trial of Jesus, a Roman provincial governor.

clue.text: Assistant from place comic upset

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sidekick emerges after a comedian is put out.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner in crime helps the main offender, so is an assistant.

clue.text: I will set down after nasty chap with current American car

indicators.note: the contraction is placed after the cad, so it follows him in the answer

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably
I'll is the contraction of I will
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Someone vows to drop a bounder off, along with the current, in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand is General Motors' luxury marque, the classic big American automobile.

clue.text: English hunt's regressive reputation

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for the hunt's gatherings is read in reverse

parts.note: a meet is a gathering of a hunt; the 's supplies the plural S

explanation.surface: An English fox hunt's reputation is said to be going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean the regard or high opinion in which someone is held by others.

clue.text: Raised issue that's against the current

parts.note: up means raised
to stream is to issue or flow out

explanation.surface: A raised issue goes against prevailing opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving towards a river's source means travelling against the flow.

clue.text: Aquatic creatures returning fight around river

indicators.note: the reversed fight wraps around the river abbreviation
going back, so the word for a fight is read backwards

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or quarrel
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Animals scrapping again on their way back up a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SETTO into OTTES, and 'around' places R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: These furry mammals live in rivers and swim superbly, so they are creatures of the water.

clue.text: Aimless motion makes Ted wild

indicators.note: the letters of the words are made into something new by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Fidgeting drives Ted mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddling idly with one's thumbs is a pointless, purposeless movement.

clue.text: Witness is able to put across artist — producer of graffiti?

indicators.note: the spy is put across the artist, straddling him, so the artist sits inside

parts.note: to spy is to see or witness
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
can means is able

explanation.surface: A witness says they can spot the artist who daubed the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Street artists use an aerosol of paint to make their wall art, so it is the tool that produces it.

clue.text: Set place to rest on lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed, a place to rest
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Someone sets a bed down beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A select social circle is a set or clique of people.

clue.text: Anne perhaps to deal with broadcast in a Scottish way

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken on air, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: Anne, the Princess Royal, daughter of Queen Elizabeth II, is an example of a royal princess; to treat a matter is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Princess Anne is about to handle a broadcast in Scottish fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a Scottish way' looks like a manner of speaking; it is the definition. Said aloud, the princess-plus-treat phrase gives the street's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Edinburgh's main shopping thoroughfare, and a street is a way or road.

clue.text: Following church after wrongdoing

indicators.note: the church goes after the wrongdoing in the answer

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone goes to church after misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means from a past time onward, that is, after.

clue.text: Those in favour will give a positive response

parts.note: yes is a positive reply

explanation.surface: Supporters will answer in the affirmative.
explanation.definitionFit: In a vote, those voting for a motion are counted as the affirmative side.

clue.text: Decline on working — showing this?

indicators.note: when letters are working they are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning down work suggests a certain trait of character.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness is what one shows by refusing to work, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Nobleman by end of party having good time

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, taken from party

explanation.surface: A peer at a party enjoys himself until it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having good time' looks like enjoying oneself; it means arriving ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ahead of schedule is to have time in hand, punctual with a margin.

clue.text: Flat race maybe failing to finish

indicators.note: the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a race is one example of an event at a sports meeting

explanation.surface: A horse race on the Flat ends with a runner not completing the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like flat racing, the British turf season without jumps; it is the definition, meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Level and smooth: a flat surface is level, with no bumps.

clue.text: Sewer of open water leading to mass anxiety

indicators.note: the first piece goes in front of what follows

parts.note: the sea is open water
m is the symbol for mass in physics
stress is anxiety or strain

explanation.surface: A drain of open water feeds widespread worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain; it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sews for a living is one who sews, a needlewoman.
